projects.title: Bacon (Columbia University's 2017 DivHacks Hackathon, 1st Place)
projects.description:
Participated in Columbia University's inaugural DivHacks hackathon and contributed to my team's winning project, Bacon, by creating an interactive prototype of our iOS app using Adobe XD (Experience Design), for the judges to demo. I was also in charge of creating all other graphics for the project, including our projects logo. Graphics created using Adobe Photoshop & Adobe Illustrator.

Bacon, a financial literacy tool for low-income minority communities, was developed in the hopes that it can help these low-income communities learn how to better manage their financial situation by teaching them how to save and create a budget. The app also educates the user on how credit and credit cards work and its many benefits, while also highlighting the potential risks in using them so that the user evades debt.

Our team believes that it is important to know how to properly manage your wealth. Managing it well can lead to many different resources becoming more accessible. One of the goals of this platform is to also get low-income communities more involved in tech, and by teaching them money management principles and strategies, they will have the tools to save up for a new laptop, phone, or tablet so they can take advantage of all the great tech resources online.

projects.title: WhatsIn (3rd Annual Lehman College NSBE Hackathon, 1st Place)
projects.description:
Competed in Lehman College's 3rd annual National Society of Black Engineers (NSBE) hackathon, and contributed to my team's winning project titled WhatsIn, by creating all graphics used on website, social media platforms, and Android application using Adobe Photoshop. I also contributed to the idea and the UI design of the Android application.

WhatsIn, a mobile and web platform created with our fellow Bronxites and the problem of malnutrition, obesity, and overall lack of healthier food options they face in mind, was developed to educate users of the chemicals that are in the foods that they purchase. A lot of our low-income communities are purchasing foods that are full of all these chemicals that have all these alternate uses that are worrying, so my team and I worked on a mobile app and website which allows users the ability to scan a food product's barcode to capture additional information on the chemicals in the ingredients list and their alternate uses.

Example: I go to the corner store (or "bodega" as I sometimes call it) and purchase a can of Coke. I scan the cans barcode and find out that the can of Coke contains Phosphoric Acid. I also find out that it's chemical formula is H3O4P, and is used as a food additive in Coke, but can also be used in medicine and as a rust remover.

This is something that worries us and could worry others if they knew. Our goal is that the user will switch to water or freshly squeezed juices after finding out the drink they have been drinking can also remove the rust on a nail.
